items.note: Both plans state B1 (net change (JV+RG)x independent of a,c), B2 (bit central coefficient |S∩T| mod 2, side wires cancel intersection one, self coefficient one), B3 (complex coefficient (|S∩T|-1)/2, side cancels intersections zero and two) and B4 (the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x)), plus the gate definitions, schedule and wire counts (A S2.2.1.1-S2.2.1.7, B S4.1.1-S4.1.10; paper 741-783).

Both give the frame invariant, its passage through pointwise gates by linearity, the operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} on all roles (A S2.2.2; B S4.2.1-S4.2.2; paper 804-825). B spells out the induction slightly more, A the linearity formula; same content.

differences.what: A lists the orthogonal residual of every edge (X: B⊗t_X^⊥, P⊗t_X^⊥; Y: B⊗t_Y^⊥, P⊗t_Y^⊥; center: B⊗F then P⊗F three times; side: B⊗<t_Y>, (B⊗t_Y^⊥)⊥(P⊗<t_X>), P⊗<t_X,t_Y>^⊥, P⊗<t_Y>; scratch sink (A⊗F)⊗Q^⊥). B gives only the gate-label table and the residuals of the side edge 2->5 and the central edge 3->4; its method names the residual table without its content.

A states that every nonzero residual contains a norm-one vector and so has an orthonormal basis, with the alternating planes absorbed through w+a, w+b, w+a+b. B states nonalternating implies an orthonormal basis but omits the plane absorption and justifies nonalternation by a 'coordinate unit vector' in the residual, which the paper does not claim (its norm-one vectors are tensors of line generators and coordinate units).

items.note: Both carry L2 (side edge 2->5 with t_X⊥t_Y and complement of dimension h-2), L3 (only center 3->4 decreases by h; telescoping to Wm-2N+2L) and L5 (100/539, 101/539). A alone carries the residual table (L1) and the complete orthonormal-basis argument (L4).

Both assign P_U to gates and sinks and -P_{U_a} to X_a sources, give rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, the N exceptional edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one, the endpoint difference I_m and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m with the shear frames Phi_M (A S2.2.4.1-S2.2.4.4; B S4.3.6.1-S4.3.6.5; paper 1115-1171).

differences.what: A states that on k columns each residual vector contributes one tensored factor acting on all k columns, s_c factors in all. B only mentions C^{⊗mk} on k columns at the endpoint, not the factor count per residual vector.

A states the endpoint frames (zero label has frame I, full label C^{⊗m}) before the X_a->Y_a repair; B has the C^{-1} on the 27 support coordinates, C=iZC^{-1}Z, Z_{a,k} and i^{27k}Z_{a,k} and the negated X outputs, but not the endpoint frames.

items.note: P1 (mod-4 weight additivity over an orthonormal residual basis) and P2 (odd weight, i^{eps[v·x]} to aI+bX_v via H diag(1,-1) H = X) are present in both. A alone has P3, and its P4 is slightly more complete.

Both have R1 (L/N<1/2, deficits N-2L_b and 2N-2L_c positive; B via the 'N more source ranks leave a strict saving' step), R2 and R3 (the exact eta values) and R4 (both above 20·2^{-50}, log m<20, s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}) (A S2.2.3.7, S2.2.4.3, S2.2.5.3, S2.2.6; B S4.3.5, S4.3.7.2, S4.4.1-S4.4.4; paper 1105-1110, 1319-1343).

Both state the four elementary O(V) stream operations and the controlled cyclic shift by splitting each fiber and merging in opposite order, with unit scaling and negation (A S2.1.1-S2.1.2; B S2-S3; paper 491-600).

differences.what: B gives the elimination proof of A=E_1 Pi E_2: the pivot at the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, clearing left by right multiplication and below by left multiplication with lower-triangular elementary matrices, scaling, deleting the pivot row and column and repeating, with pivots counting the rank. A names only the pivot choice and the result with exactly a ones.

items.note: M2 (fixed odd prime avoiding the table's denominators, so the identities specialize to Z/q^b), M3 (lower-triangular transformation in O(V) in descending order) and M4 (D_j<-D_j+H_i, interchange, D_j<-H_i-D_j; a interchanges) are in both. B alone carries the full elimination mechanism (M1).

Both carry the cyclic row split into W role streams of volume V/W, shear frames Phi_{A_e} by recursive interchanges, H<-H+D on every row including scratch rows, the three-shear interchange, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) solved to O(e^tau), the parking-stack schedule and the descriptor-work bound (A S2.3.2.1-S2.3.2.7; B S4.5.2.1-S4.5.2.8.3; paper 1491-1616).

Both borrow rho=ceil(k log W/(2 log q)) high digits as a row field of range at least W^k, pad rows below 2V, split the rest in base m with the geometric sum O(Ve^tau), pad binary ranges to q^e and handle widths differing by one bit (A S2.3.3.1-S2.3.3.4; B S4.5.3.1-S4.5.3.8; paper 1649-1762). B lists the field orders in more detail; same steps.

Both give the C identities, the conjugation P_M X_v P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv} and the coordinate form of the edge change, one child per kernel on f axes, a negative kernel via (C^{-1})^{⊗f}=(-i)^f Z^{⊗f} C^{⊗f} Z^{⊗f}, at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, exactly s_c children, and H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D (A S2.4.1.1-S2.4.1.6; B S4.6.1.1-S4.6.1.8; paper 1806-1940).

differences.what: A states that the omitted top selected position j_{f-1} is handled by one two-bit XOR in O(V), and that this is the whole algorithm when f=1. B omits the top position from the segments but never says how it is supplied.

items.note: Both carry the eight updates and parity cycles, the whole-chunk cyclic shifts as bijections, the guard interval and delta_bad bound, the repair of T_0 S_0^{-1} on the bad set by radix sort, the swap/rotation count and the cost (paper 2013-2231). A alone covers the case of the top position.

Both give individual kernels at O(Ve), node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)) with s children, the q_0 row chunks and padding to W^{k_0}, children of exactly 1/W volume, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves at e<d^beta, the internal and leaf sums, and the base-m groups giving O(d^{lambda'}) (A S2.4.3.1-S2.4.3.7; B S4.6.3.1-S4.6.3.11; paper 2283-2448).

differences.what: B carries the proposition's uniformity check: Delta<=p so R_g=2r(p+2Delta+3)<=12rp, A_*<=C_A p with C_A=C_M+b_r+7, and the two extra normalized packed-call terms tending to zero, giving one constant for every packed child; it also states the proposition's parameter conditions. A has neither.

items.note: All five checklist sub-steps are present in both: S1 (E, B, nu, C_1, C_0, Delta, with nu=11, C_1=20), S2 (A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, A(e)<=8e, per-invocation count 24W^3+4s+4W+4<E), S3 (B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^nu, total <C_0 d^{C_1}), S4 (depth to bits, epsilon C_1<1 gives Delta=o(p)) and S5 (absolute row sum one, truncation error below sqrt2 2^{-p}). B adds the uniform-cost check from the proof.

Both carry character cancellation without division, decimation in frequency into bit-reversed order, the reversed procedure for F^+B^{-1}, a round as H then J_E, the layout L (prefix slots, chunk-major exchanges), simultaneous layers per round, prefix rounds, monomial implementation, J_E Q_p = Q_p J_E, error sqrt2 l 2^{-p} and the exact operators LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1} (A S3.1.1-S3.1.2.7; B S5.1-S5.2.9; paper 2776-3206).

Both carry evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, the |h_j|<B_0/2 bound and centered-residue extraction with carry in {0,1}, negacyclic reduction with |H_j|<=r 2^{2p}, the final shift by p+l, and four products dominating the cost (A S3.1.4.1-S3.1.4.5; B S5.3.1-S5.3.7; paper 3233-3368).

Both carry the commutation of pointwise products with LB, the normalization identity, the error chain 2delta+eta then 3delta+eta times M = sqrt2 M(3l+1) 2^{-p}, and the cost with M=T/r products (A S3.1, S3.1.3, S3.1.5-S3.1.7; B S5, S5.4.1-S5.4.7; paper 3414-3495).

differences.what: B defines the retained permutations (P_s u)_j=u_{tj}, (P_t v)_k=v_{-sk} and the two Gaussian maps S, T; A uses P_s, P_t, R, Q and S, T without ever defining them.

items.note: Both carry the identity TP_sF_s=P_tF_tS, N=CTD with ||N-I||<1/2 and the Neumann series, the contractions A and B_0 with the 2^{2alpha^2} normalization, the error and time bounds, the avoided sorts, the tensor form, and axis exposure (paper 3576-3897). B also defines the permutations that are left in the transform.

Both give the chirp identity QF_t u = conj(a)·(a*(conj(a)·u))/T with the coefficient check, and the cancellation (RF_s^+)[(RF_s u)·(RF_s v)]=(u*v)/S^2 via F_s^+R=R^{-1}F_s^+, the commutation with pointwise products and the two normalizations, plus RF_s^+ by conjugation (A S3.3, S3.4; B S7.1.1-S7.3, S8.5.4; paper 3938-3988).

differences.what: A verifies that the fixed constants satisfy the layer conditions (tau(1+c/beta)<1-31·2^{-55}<lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)=1-2^{-51}<lambda<lambda'<1) and the dimension conditions, and fixes the band constants a_d=a_r=1/12, b_d=1, b_r=1/3 from b/2<=log2 T<=b, giving K/log p->infinity. B lists the constants but checks neither.

items.note: Both carry the constants, sizes, alpha, gamma=o(b), the prime-interval count, distinct odd primes, T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta_i>p and the n^{o(1)} search (paper 4004-4170). A also verifies the conditions that make the lemmas' hypotheses hold.

Both carry Phi as an isomorphism (image of x of order S), the triangular coordinate formula b_i=a_i+mu_i sum_{j<i} a_j P_j, padding scan, rotations of valid intervals that keep zero padding zero, and the O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)) cost (A S3.5.3.1-S3.5.3.5; B S8.3.1-S8.3.7; paper 4204-4296).

Both give Theta: x_d -> zeta y as a diagonal isomorphism, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, and M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T, with the computed twists (A S3.5.4-S3.5.5, S3.5.9.2; B S8.4.1-S8.4.5, S8.7.2; paper 4298-4413).

Both carry the computed chirp transform, the source transform with exact counterpart 2^gamma B_0 QF_t A=RF_s and its conjugate, and the six steps with scales S and 2^{2b+4}S undoing the two normalizations (A S3.5.6-S3.5.8; B S8.5-S8.6.7; paper 4415-4544).

Both chain E_ring<5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s=9·2^gamma TL, (2E_s+2), (3E_s+2), E_w<28·2^gamma T^2 L, the final 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2, rounding and the carry recurrence (A S3.5.9-S3.5.10.5; B S8.7-S8.8.10; paper 4546-4806).

Both tabulate the normalized costs and powers, the seven margins with minimum g_2=2^{-181}=2kappa, the per-row justifications, setup and exceptional streams o(V), and the final O(n(log n)^{1-kappa}) with a schoolbook cutoff (A S4.1-S4.9; B S9.1-S9.4.3; paper 4808-4995).

differences.what: A states that refuting the conjecture needs one machine with liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0, and that the bound O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) sends the ratio to zero through all lengths. B's S1 only recounts the history (Schonhage-Strassen's proposal, Harvey-van der Hoeven's O(n log n)), and its S0 makes no refutation claim.

items.note: Only A carries the logic that turns the time bound into a refutation of the n log n lower bound in the fixed-tape model.

chain.note: Both trees follow the paper's route: the exchange network, then frames, then nested labels with s=Wm-N+2L or Wm-2N+2L<Wm, then s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, then the two recurrences (interchange O(Ve^tau), layer O(Vd^{lambda'})), then the transforms, resampling, chirp, CRT and assembly, then the cost table to O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}), and neither breaks. The differences (A's residual table and k-column factor count, B's elimination detail) are completeness within items, not breaks in the dependency chain.

errors.says: Each nonzero residual over F_2 is nonalternating because it contains a coordinate unit vector of norm one.
errors.paper: The residual's norm-one vector is a tensor of chosen norm-one vectors: line generators of P and Q, and coordinate units only in B, Q^perp, triple complements and full factors. A residual such as P⊗F⊗Q contains no coordinate unit vector of F^{⊗3}.

errors.says: At a node, the s children plus the binary basis changes, scalar gates, endpoint corrections and reassembly cost O(V((eK)^tau+1)) at that node.
errors.paper: The O(V((eK)^tau+1)) bound covers only the non-recursive work at the node. The s recursive calls are charged separately through the (s/W)F(e/m) term. B's S4.6.3.7 states the recurrence correctly, so this may be loose wording.

errors.says: The multiplication algorithm obtains the exact 2n-bit product in O(Tp) steps beyond the layer costs.
errors.paper: The non-layer stages cost more than O(Tp). Normalized by Tp they are d^2(1+l^tau) for the CRT and axis layouts, dp^{1/2+delta}alpha for the Gaussian line maps, dp^delta for the chirps, log(rp) for the packed products and p^delta for the final scaling (Table tab:costs).

overall.reason: Neither plan has a major error, and both reconstruct the central chain in full. On the core of the saving, A carries the per-edge residual table (L1), the complete orthonormal-basis argument (L4) and the k-column factor count (P3), which B lacks; B carries only the elimination detail of M1, the layer's uniform packed-cost check and the definitions of P_s, P_t. A also has the refutation logic and the condition checks on the parameters. B has three minor misstatements (coordinate unit vectors in residuals, children folded into the node overhead, O(Tp) beyond the layer costs), so the balance tips slightly to A.
